question: I am a poor woman in a village and want to join a women's group that saves money together and can get a low-interest bank loan so I can start a small business. Which government programme supports this?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Meant for rural poor households: at least one member of each identified poor household, preferably a woman, is brought into a Self Help Group.
- Poor households are identified by the community through the Participatory Identification of Poor (PIP) process, and the list is vetted by the Gram Sabha; the BPL list alone is not used.
- SHGs usually have 10 to 20 members, mostly women; special SHGs in remote tribal or difficult areas, or of vulnerable people such as persons with disabilities, may have as few as 5 members.
- Groups of persons with disabilities, elderly people or transgender persons may include both men and women; other SHGs are women's groups.
- To get the Revolving Fund, an SHG should have existed for at least 3 to 6 months, follow the Panchasutras and not have received a Revolving Fund before.
- To get a bank loan, an SHG must have been active for at least 6 months as per its books of account and follow the Panchasutras: regular meetings, regular savings, regular inter-loaning, timely repayment and up-to-date books.
- The SHG must qualify under the grading norms fixed by NABARD.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The poorest, single women, women-headed households, persons with disabilities, landless people and migrant labourers get special focus.
Not eligible:
- The mission is for rural areas; the interest subvention is only for women SHGs in rural areas.
- An SHG that has already received a Revolving Fund earlier cannot get it again.
- Interest subvention is given only while the SHG loan account stays in the standard (regularly repaid) category.
- A defunct SHG can get credit only after it is revived and stays active for at least 3 months.

Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) — Overview
DAY-NRLM brings at least one member of each poor rural household, preferably a woman, into a Self Help Group (SHG). It then supports these groups with a Revolving Fund of Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, community investment funds, bank loans without collateral, interest subvention and training. The mission is ongoing and is run by the Ministry of Rural Development through State Rural Livelihoods Missions.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development.

- Training and capacity building for members, plus self-employment training through Rural Self Employment Training Institutes (RSETIs) and help to access insurance.

question: What is the minimum age to register on e-Shram?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Eligibility rules
- Works in the unorganised sector as a home-based worker, self-employed worker or wage worker. This also covers someone in an organised-sector job who is not covered by EPFO or ESIC and is not a government employee.
- Aged 16 years or older at the time of registration.
- Not a member of EPFO or ESIC.
- Not a member of the government-funded National Pension System (NPS).
- Not an income tax payer.
- Has an Aadhaar number and a mobile number, preferably linked with Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Members of EPFO or ESIC cannot register.
- Members of the government-funded NPS cannot register.
- Income tax payers cannot register.
- Government employees are not counted as unorganised workers.
- Persons below 16 years of age cannot register.

e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — How to apply
- Self-register online on the e-Shram portal (register.eshram.gov.in) using Aadhaar e-KYC, or through the UMANG mobile app.
- Or register at the nearest Common Service Centre (CSC) or State Seva Kendra. State Government field officers also help at district and sub-district level.
- Registration is free of cost, and no agency or centre may charge a fee.
- Helpline: 14434 or 1800-889-6811 (9 am to 6 pm every day, including Sundays). Grievances can be filed at gms.eshram.gov.in.

e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Overview
A free, one-time registration for unorganised workers aged 16 and above. It gives a 12-digit UAN e-Shram card and a single window for linked welfare schemes such as PMSBY accident insurance and the PM-SYM pension. Registering does not by itself pay any cash.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Labour and Employment.

question: How much accident insurance can an e-Shram card holder get through PMSBY?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 to 70 years.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can be covered through only one account, even if they have several.
- In a joint account, each holder who meets the conditions can join by paying Rs 20 each.
Not eligible:
- Cover ends on reaching age 70 (age nearest birthday).
- Cover ends if the bank account is closed or does not have enough balance to pay the premium.
- Only accidents are covered; death by suicide is not covered, though murder is.
- If enrolled through more than one account, the extra premium is forfeited and cover is given through one account only.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Overview
A one-year accident insurance, renewed every year, for bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 70. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year taken automatically from the account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Benefits
- Rs 2 lakh on death due to an accident.
- Rs 2 lakh for total and permanent loss of both eyes, both hands or both feet, or of one eye together with one hand or foot.
- Rs 1 lakh for permanent loss of one eye or of one hand or foot (partial disability).
- The premium is Rs 20 a year, auto-debited from the account in one instalment.
- Cover lasts one year, from 1 June to 31 May, is renewed every year, and is in addition to any other insurance the person has.

question: e-Shram card wale ko PMSBY me kitna accident bima mil sakta hai?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 to 70 years.
- Holds an individual or joint savings account with a participating bank or post office.
- Agrees to join and allows the yearly premium to be auto-debited from that account.
- A person can be covered through only one account, even if they have several.
- In a joint account, each holder who meets the conditions can join by paying Rs 20 each.
Not eligible:
- Cover ends on reaching age 70 (age nearest birthday).
- Cover ends if the bank account is closed or does not have enough balance to pay the premium.
- Only accidents are covered; death by suicide is not covered, though murder is.
- If enrolled through more than one account, the extra premium is forfeited and cover is given through one account only.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Overview
A one-year accident insurance, renewed every year, for bank or post office account holders aged 18 to 70. It pays Rs 2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh for partial disability, for a premium of Rs 20 a year taken automatically from the account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) — Benefits
- Rs 2 lakh on death due to an accident.
- Rs 2 lakh for total and permanent loss of both eyes, both hands or both feet, or of one eye together with one hand or foot.
- Rs 1 lakh for permanent loss of one eye or of one hand or foot (partial disability).
- The premium is Rs 20 a year, auto-debited from the account in one instalment.
- Cover lasts one year, from 1 June to 31 May, is renewed every year, and is in addition to any other insurance the person has.

answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

e-Shram (National Database of Unorganised Workers) (e-Shram) — Eligibility rules
- Works in the unorganised sector as a home-based worker, self-employed worker or wage worker. This also covers someone in an organised-sector job who is not covered by EPFO or ESIC and is not a government employee.
- Aged 16 years or older at the time of registration.

- Government employees are not counted as unorganised workers.
- Persons below 16 years of age cannot register.

Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) — Eligibility rules
- Joined an establishment covered by EPF between 1 August 2025 and 31 July 2027 (both dates included).
- Is a first-time EPF member, meaning they never contributed to EPF with EPFO or an exempted PF trust before 1 August 2025.
- Has a gross monthly salary of up to Rs 1,00,000 at the time of joining, counting all emoluments.
- Has worked at least 6 completed months in the same establishment (needed for the first instalment).
- Has worked 12 completed months in the same establishment and finished the free online financial literacy course (needed for the second instalment).
- Has a UAN and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Anyone who contributed to EPF, with EPFO or an exempted trust, before 1 August 2025 is not a first-timer and cannot get the incentive.
- Employees whose gross monthly salary is above Rs 1,00,000 at joining are not covered.
- Anyone who leaves the job before 6 completed months gets no first instalment.
- Anyone who leaves between 6 and 12 months does not get the second instalment.

Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) — How to apply
- Employees do not need to apply or register. The incentive is worked out from the monthly PF return (ECR) that the employer files.
- Get a UAN through the employer, or generate it yourself using face authentication on the UMANG app.
- Make sure your bank account is seeded with Aadhaar. Payment is held back until it is.
- Before completing 12 months, finish the free financial literacy course on the EPFO website. Helpline: 14480 or 1800-180-1850 (toll-free).

- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).

Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK) — Eligibility rules
- Any pregnant woman who gives birth in a public (government) health institution.

Makes childbirth, including caesarean section, and care for pregnancy complications completely free in government health facilities. This includes free medicines, tests, blood, food and transport. Sick newborns and infants up to 1 year of age get similar free care in public facilities.

question: जननी शिशु सुरक्षा कार्यक्रम में नॉर्मल डिलीवरी के बाद कितने दिन तक खाना मुफ्त मिलता है?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be identified by its State/UT government as a Priority Household (PHH) and hold an NFSA ration card.
- Each state sets its own criteria for priority households, so the rules differ from state to state.
- Nationally, up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population can be covered; each state has its own coverage percentage.
- The eldest woman of the household aged 18 years or more is named head of the household on the ration card; if there is no such woman, the eldest man is head until a female member turns 18.
- The Centre has told states to include eligible persons with disabilities, persons affected by leprosy and children born after 2011.
Not eligible:
- Households not identified by the state as priority households or Antyodaya households are not covered.
- Total coverage in each state is fixed using Census 2011 figures; the ceiling can be raised only after data from the next census is published.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Benefits
- Every member of a priority household is entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains (rice, wheat or coarse grains) per person per month.
- Under PMGKAY the grain is given free of cost, so there is nothing to pay at the ration shop.
- Free grain started on 1 January 2023, and the Centre decided to continue it for five years starting 1 January 2024.
- The prices fixed in the Act before free distribution were Rs 3 per kg for rice, Rs 2 per kg for wheat and Rs 1 per kg for coarse grains.
- Under One Nation One Ration Card, the grain can be taken from any ePoS-enabled ration shop in India.
- If the state does not supply the entitled grain, the person can claim a food security allowance from the state government.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Overview
Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, every member of a household that the state identifies as a Priority Household gets 5 kg of foodgrains a month from the ration shop. Under PMGKAY this grain is free of cost, and the Centre has continued it for five years from 1 January 2024. States decide which households qualify, within coverage limits of up to 75% of rural and 50% of urban people nationally.
Central government scheme. Department of Food and Public Distribution, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution.

question: We are a family of five living on daily wages and we have no ration card. How can each of us get free wheat or rice every month from the ration shop?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Eligibility rules
- The household must be identified by its State/UT government as a Priority Household (PHH) and hold an NFSA ration card.
- Each state sets its own criteria for priority households, so the rules differ from state to state.
- Nationally, up to 75% of the rural population and up to 50% of the urban population can be covered; each state has its own coverage percentage.
- The eldest woman of the household aged 18 years or more is named head of the household on the ration card; if there is no such woman, the eldest man is head until a female member turns 18.
- The Centre has told states to include eligible persons with disabilities, persons affected by leprosy and children born after 2011.
Not eligible:
- Households not identified by the state as priority households or Antyodaya households are not covered.
- Total coverage in each state is fixed using Census 2011 figures; the ceiling can be raised only after data from the next census is published.
- Ineligible, fake or duplicate ration cards, and members who have died or migrated, are removed when states verify their lists.

National Food Security Act, 2013 - Priority Households, with Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) (NFSA / PMGKAY) — Benefits
- Every member of a priority household is entitled to 5 kg of foodgrains (rice, wheat or coarse grains) per person per month.
- Under PMGKAY the grain is given free of cost, so there is nothing to pay at the ration shop.
- Free grain started on 1 January 2023, and the Centre decided to continue it for five years starting 1 January 2024.
- The prices fixed in the Act before free distribution were Rs 3 per kg for rice, Rs 2 per kg for wheat and Rs 1 per kg for coarse grains.
- Under One Nation One Ration Card, the grain can be taken from any ePoS-enabled ration shop in India.
- If the state does not supply the entitled grain, the person can claim a food security allowance from the state government.

Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Meant for the poorest of the poor households, identified by the State/UT government under the AAY guidelines.
- Landless agricultural labourers, marginal farmers, and rural artisans or craftsmen such as potters, tanners, weavers, blacksmiths and carpenters.
- Slum dwellers, destitute persons, and people earning a daily living in the informal sector, such as porters, coolies, rickshaw pullers, hand-cart pullers, fruit and flower sellers, snake charmers, rag pickers and cobblers, in rural or urban areas.
- Households headed by a widow, a terminally ill or disabled person, or a person aged 60 years or more, with no assured means of living or social support.
- Widows, terminally ill or disabled persons, persons aged 60 years or more, and single women or single men who have no family or social support and no assured income.
- All primitive tribal households.
- Eligible BPL families with an HIV-positive member are to be included on priority.
- Up to 2.5 crore poorest families can be covered across the country, within ceilings fixed for each state.

question: How much money does Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana give a TB patient every month?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Eligibility rules
- You must be a TB (tuberculosis) patient who is notified (registered) on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Patients treated in the private sector qualify too, as long as they are notified on Ni-kshay.
- New, previously treated and drug-resistant TB patients are all covered.
- There is no age or income limit; all notified TB patients are beneficiaries.
- Children with TB are covered; if the child has no bank account, the money goes to a parent's or guardian's account.
- Patients notified on or after 1 April 2018, and those already on treatment on that date, are eligible.
Not eligible:
- A TB patient who is not notified on the Ni-kshay portal cannot receive the payment.
- Payments are only for the period the patient is on anti-TB treatment; they stop when treatment ends.

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Overview
Gives every TB patient registered (notified) on the Ni-kshay portal money every month for nutritious food for the whole time they are on TB treatment, paid by direct bank transfer. The amount was raised from Rs 500 to Rs 1,000 per month in late 2024.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (Central TB Division, National TB Elimination Programme).

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Benefits
- Rs 1,000 per month for as long as the patient is on TB treatment (raised from Rs 500 per month; increase announced in late 2024).
- Money is paid by Direct Benefit Transfer into the bank account, preferably an Aadhaar-linked account.
- Under the 2018 payment schedule, the first payment comes when the patient is notified, and later payments come at follow-up points during treatment (for a new patient: at about 2 months and at the end of 6 months).
- If treatment is extended, payment continues for the extra months.
- Some states may give a food basket of at least the same value instead of cash, with central approval.

question: निक्षय पोषण योजना में टीबी मरीज़ को हर महीने कितने रुपये मिलते हैं?

Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) — Eligibility rules
- Aged 18 years or above.
- Has a severe disability of 80% or more, or multiple disabilities (two or more disabilities together).
- Persons with dwarfism are also eligible.
- Must belong to a household below the poverty line (BPL).
- If the name is missing from the BPL list but the person is otherwise deserving, officials are told not to leave them out and to check and establish eligibility.

A monthly central pension for people aged 18 or above with severe (80% or more) or multiple disabilities from below-poverty-line (BPL) households: Rs 300 a month up to age 79 and Rs 500 a month from age 80. Many states add their own amount on top.

question: My son is in Class 8 at a government school and our family income is about 2 lakh a year. Is there an exam he can write to get a scholarship every year until Class 12?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Parents' income from all sources must be no more than Rs 3,50,000 a year.
- You need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 7 exam to sit the selection test. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must study as a regular student in a government, government-aided or local body school.
- You must pass the state's selection test in Class 8 (Mental Ability Test and Scholastic Aptitude Test) with at least 40% marks in aggregate. The cut-off for SC/ST students is 32%.
- At the time of selection you need at least 55% marks (or an equivalent grade) in the Class 8 exam. SC/ST students get a 5% relaxation.
- You must be promoted from Class 8 to Class 9 to start receiving the scholarship.
- To continue, you must pass Class 9 and Class 11 in the first attempt, and you need at least 60% marks in Class 10 (5% lower for SC/ST students).
Not eligible:
- Students of Kendriya Vidyalayas and Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas.
- Students of residential schools run by Central or State Government institutions that provide boarding, lodging and education.
- Students of private schools.
- Diploma or certificate-level courses and studies abroad are not covered.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- A student can hold only one Central Government scholarship.
- The scholarship stops if there is a gap of one academic session, and once stopped it cannot be restarted.

National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (NMMSS) — Overview
A central scholarship of Rs 12,000 a year for bright students from low-income families studying in Class 9 to 12 in government, government-aided and local body schools. Students are chosen through a state-level test taken in Class 8, and 1,00,000 new scholarships are given every year.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education, Department of School Education and Literacy.

question: What is the minimum amount needed to open an NPS Vatsalya account?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

NPS Vatsalya — Eligibility rules
- The child must be below 18 years of age (17 or younger) when the account is opened.
- Open to Indian citizens under 18, including Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) and Overseas Citizens of India (OCIs).
- A parent or legal guardian opens and runs the account in the child's name. The child is the only beneficiary.
- The minimum contribution is Rs 250 to open the account and at least Rs 250 in each financial year. There is no upper limit.
- For an NRI or OCI child, a bank account must be given (the minor's own or joint NRE/NRO account).
Not eligible:
- Anyone who has already turned 18 cannot open an NPS Vatsalya account. They can join the regular NPS instead.

NPS Vatsalya — Overview
A long-term savings and pension account under the National Pension System that a parent or guardian opens in the name of a child under 18, with as little as Rs 250 a year. When the child turns 18, they can move the money to a regular NPS account or take part of it out, and they can withdraw it all if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

NPS Vatsalya — How to apply
- Open online on the eNPS platform of NPS Trust (npstrust.org.in) or through the online service of a Point of Presence.
- Or visit a Point of Presence registered with PFRDA, such as a bank, India Post or a pension fund.
- When opening the account, the guardian chooses a Central Recordkeeping Agency and a pension fund. Parents, relatives and friends can then pay in by cash, cheque or online.
- At 18, the young person must complete fresh KYC and give nominee details before any withdrawal or change is allowed.

Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance (Department of Financial Services); regulated and administered by PFRDA.

NPS Vatsalya — Benefits
- A pension fund registered with PFRDA, chosen by the guardian, invests the money. Returns are market-linked, with an indicative 50% to 75% in equity.
- Partial withdrawals are allowed only after 3 years from opening the account. You can take out up to 25% of the money paid in (not the returns) for the child's education, treatment of specified illnesses, or disability of more than 75%.

- At 18 the account can continue for up to 3 more years. After fresh KYC, the young person has three choices: move the full amount into regular NPS (All Citizen Model), take up to 80% as a lump sum and use the rest to buy an annuity, or withdraw everything if the total is less than Rs 8 lakh.
- If no choice is made by age 21, the account moves to a higher-equity scheme of the same pension fund and follows regular NPS rules.
- If the child dies, the entire amount saved is paid to the guardian, nominee or legal heirs.

question: Meri beti 10 saal ki hai, main uske naam par lambi avadhi ka pension khata kholna chahta hoon jisme saal me kam se kam thoda paisa daal sakoon. Kaun si sarkari yojana hai?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) — Eligibility rules
- Works in the unorganised sector, for example as a street vendor, domestic worker, rickshaw puller, head loader, construction or farm labourer, beedi, handloom or leather worker, or in similar work.
- Aged 18 to 40 when joining.
- Monthly income of Rs 15,000 or less.
- Has an Aadhaar card and a savings bank or Jan Dhan account with IFSC.
Not eligible:
- People older than 40 cannot join.
- Members of EPFO, ESIC or NPS (organised-sector coverage) cannot join.
- Income tax payers cannot join.
- People already getting benefits from another government pension scheme are not eligible, according to the PIB note on the scheme.

Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM) — Benefits
- A minimum assured pension of Rs 3,000 per month for life from age 60.
- The worker pays Rs 55 to Rs 200 a month depending on age at joining (Rs 55 at 18, Rs 105 at 30, Rs 200 at 40) until age 60, and the Central Government adds an equal amount every month.
- If the pensioner dies, the spouse gets 50% of the pension as family pension; family pension is only for the spouse.
- If the member dies before 60 after paying regularly, the spouse can continue the scheme and later get the pension, or take back the member's contribution with interest.
- Leaving within 10 years returns the worker's own contribution with savings bank interest; leaving after 10 years but before 60 returns it with the interest earned by the fund or savings bank interest, whichever is higher.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maan-Dhan Yojana (PM-KMY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Small or marginal farmer who owns cultivable land of up to 2 hectares as per state or UT land records.
- Aged 18 to 40 years at the time of joining.
- Name must appear in the state or UT land records as on 01.08.2019.
- Both men and women farmers can join, in any state or union territory.
- Must agree to pay a monthly contribution of Rs 55 to Rs 200, depending on age at joining, until age 60.
Not eligible:
- Farmers already covered by another statutory social security scheme such as NPS, ESIC or an EPFO scheme.
- Farmers who have joined PM Shram Yogi Maan-Dhan (PM-SYM) or PM Laghu Vyapari Maan-Dhan (PM-LVM).
- Institutional landholders, and present or former holders of constitutional posts, Union or State ministers, MPs, MLAs, MLCs, mayors of municipal corporations and district panchayat chairpersons.
- Serving or retired officers and employees of Central or State Government, PSUs and government autonomous bodies, and regular local body employees (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D are not excluded).
- Anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year.

question: How much money does PM-KISAN give a farmer family in a year?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family must own cultivable land, and the names must be entered in the state or UT land records.
- For this scheme a farmer family means husband, wife and minor children.
- There is no upper limit on land size; the original 2-hectare cap was dropped when the scheme was opened to all landholding farmer families.
- Eligibility is judged on land ownership recorded as on 01.02.2019; land received later by inheritance after the owner's death still counts, but land bought or gifted after that date does not make the new owner eligible.
- An Aadhaar number and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar are compulsory.
- e-KYC must be completed before payments are released.
- In some North-Eastern states and in Jharkhand, land certificates from village authorities or verified lineage records are accepted where regular land records do not exist.
Not eligible:
- Institutional landholders, and (for newly added beneficiaries) Non-Resident Indians as defined under the Income Tax Act.
- Families where any member holds or has held a constitutional post, or is or was a Union or State minister, MP, MLA, MLC, mayor of a municipal corporation or chairperson of a district panchayat.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Families where any member is a serving or retired officer or employee of the Central or State Government, a central or state PSU or a government autonomous body, or a regular employee of a local body; Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D staff are not excluded.
- Families with a retired pensioner whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D pensioners are not excluded).
- Families where any member paid income tax in the last assessment year.
- Families with a practising professional registered with a professional body: doctor, engineer, lawyer, chartered accountant or architect.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Benefits
- Rs 6,000 per year for each eligible farmer family.
- The money comes in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 each, one every four months (April-July, August-November and December-March).
- Payments go by Direct Benefit Transfer straight into the family's Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
- The Central Government bears the full cost; the farmer pays nothing.

question: मेरे नाम पर खेती की ज़मीन है। क्या सरकार किसानों के बैंक खाते में हर साल सीधे पैसे भेजती है, और मुझे यह कैसे मिलेगा?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Eligibility rules
- Farmers who own and cultivate land, either alone or jointly.
- Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers.
- Self Help Groups or Joint Liability Groups of farmers, including groups of tenant farmers and sharecroppers.
- Dairy, poultry, sheep, goat, pig and rabbit farmers with their own, rented or leased sheds, individually, jointly or in groups.
- Fishers and fish farmers who own or lease a pond, tank, open water body, hatchery or registered fishing boat and hold the required fishing licence.
Not eligible:
- Only one KCC per farmer: the application asks you to declare that you have no KCC from another bank branch.
- If you already have a combined KCC for crops and allied activities, a separate livestock or fisheries KCC is not issued; the existing limit is raised instead.

Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Overview
A revolving bank loan account with a RuPay card that farmers, tenant farmers, sharecroppers, livestock keepers and fishers can use for farming costs. Under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme, short-term loans up to Rs 3 lakh carry 7% interest, which drops to 4% if repaid on time.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Credit Division); loans given by banks under RBI rules.

Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Individual farmers, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups can apply.
- Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs) and their federations, Self Help Groups and their federations, and Joint Liability Groups can apply.
- Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), marketing and multipurpose cooperative societies, and national and state federations of cooperatives can apply.
- APMCs, State agencies, and PPP projects sponsored by Central, State or local bodies can apply.
- The loan must be for an eligible post-harvest management project or community farming asset, such as warehouses, cold storage, sorting and grading units, primary processing, or smart and precision farming infrastructure.
- The applicant must put in at least 10% of the fixed project cost as own contribution (margin).
- A private applicant can get benefits for up to 25 projects, each in a different village or town with its own LGD code.
Not eligible:
- Standalone secondary processing units are not eligible.
- Tractors and non-refrigerated transport vehicles cannot be financed for individual farmers.

question: How much loan do I get the first time under PM SVANidhi?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a street vendor who sells goods or services to the public on streets, footpaths or other public places, from a temporary stall or by moving from place to place; seasonal or year-round, mobile or stationary.
- Must be an adult aged 18 years or above; there is no upper age limit.
- Vendors in cities and towns must hold a Certificate of Vending (CoV), Identity Card or Letter of Recommendation (LoR) issued by the Urban Local Body or Town Vending Committee.
- Vendors in census towns and peri-urban areas must have an LoR approved by the Block Development Officer (BDO).
- The 2nd and 3rd loans are given only after the previous loan is fully repaid.
- For the credit card only: must have repaid the 2nd loan and be eligible for or have taken the 3rd loan, and be aged 21 to 65 years.
Not eligible:
- People below 18 years of age.
- A lender may refuse the loan if the applicant has an existing loan classified as NPA or written off by any lender (a low credit score alone is not a reason to refuse).
- Manually issued LoRs are not valid; the LoR must be issued through the PM SVANidhi portal.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Benefits
- Working capital loans without collateral in three tranches: 1st loan of up to Rs 15,000 (repay in 12 months), 2nd loan of up to Rs 25,000 (repay in 18 months) and 3rd loan of up to Rs 50,000 (repay in 36 months).
- Interest subsidy of 7% per year, credited to the borrower's account every quarter; for example, up to Rs 603 on a Rs 15,000 first loan repaid on time.
- Cashback on digital transactions: Rs 1 per transaction, up to Rs 100 a month and up to Rs 1,200 a year in each tranche.
- Extra cashback of up to Rs 100 a quarter (maximum Rs 400 a year) for digital wholesale purchases of at least Rs 2,000.
- No processing fee on the 1st and 2nd loans, no margin money, no guarantee fee and no penalty for early repayment.
- A lifetime-free, UPI-linked RuPay credit card with a limit of up to Rs 30,000 (starting at Rs 10,000), valid for 5 years.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Overview
PM SVANidhi gives street vendors working capital loans without collateral in three steps: up to Rs 15,000, then Rs 25,000, then Rs 50,000. It also gives a 7% interest subsidy, cashback on digital payments and a RuPay credit card for vendors who repay well. New loans can be given until 31 March 2030 under the restructured scheme.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (with Department of Financial Services).

question: I sell vegetables from a handcart in my town and need about 15,000 rupees to buy stock, but I have nothing to give as security. Which government loan can I get?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Eligibility rules
- Meant for micro enterprises (small businesses) that need institutional credit.
- The loan must be for a non-agricultural activity; allied activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping are also covered.
- The loan can be for a term loan, working capital, or both.
- Tarun Plus loans (above Rs 10 lakh) are only for entrepreneurs who took and fully repaid an earlier loan under the Tarun category.
Not eligible:
- Farming itself is not covered; the loan is for non-agricultural purposes and allied activities only.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Overview
Loans without collateral for micro enterprises doing non-farm business, or allied activities such as poultry, dairy and beekeeping. Banks, NBFCs and microfinance institutions give the loans in four categories: Shishu (up to Rs 50,000), Kishore (up to Rs 5 lakh), Tarun (up to Rs 10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (up to Rs 20 lakh, for those who repaid a Tarun loan).
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) — Benefits
- Shishu: loan of up to Rs 50,000.
- Kishore: loan above Rs 50,000 and up to Rs 5 lakh.
- Tarun: loan above Rs 5 lakh and up to Rs 10 lakh.
- Tarun Plus: loan above Rs 10 lakh and up to Rs 20 lakh, available from 24 October 2024 to those who repaid an earlier Tarun loan.
- No collateral (security) is required.

- Farmers who own and cultivate land, either alone or jointly.

- Manually issued LoRs are not valid; the LoR must be issued through the PM SVANidhi portal.

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — Overview
PM SVANidhi gives street vendors working capital loans without collateral in three steps: up to Rs 15,000, then Rs 25,000, then Rs 50,000. It also gives a 7% interest subsidy, cashback on digital payments and a RuPay credit card for vendors who repay well. New loans can be given until 31 March 2030 under the restructured scheme.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (with Department of Financial Services).

PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi (PM SVANidhi) (PM SVANidhi) — How to apply
- Apply online on the PM SVANidhi portal (pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in) or the PM SVANidhi mobile app; new loans can be given until 31 March 2030.
- Vendors without a CoV or ID card submit a 'LoR cum loan application'; the ULB or Block office verifies it and issues the LoR digitally, and the loan request then goes to the chosen bank.
- Help is available at ULB offices, Block offices, Common Service Centres (CSCs) and from resource persons appointed by ULBs.
- Linking your mobile number with Aadhaar is advised for smooth processing.

question: I got admission to a good engineering college but my family cannot pay the fees and we have no property to pledge. How can I get an education loan without collateral or a guarantor?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Eligibility rules
- Has secured admission in a Quality Higher Educational Institution (QHEI) identified by the Ministry of Education.
- Admission should be on merit, for example through a recognised entrance exam or the merit quota.
- To get the 3% interest subvention, annual family income must be Rs 8 lakh or less, and the subvention applies to loans up to Rs 10 lakh.
- The 3% interest subvention is limited to 1 lakh students a year, chosen in this order of preference: admission to a government institution, then technical/professional courses, then students who passed Class 12 or Class 10 from a government school, then those who passed Class 12 from a rural school, then girl students.
- Aadhaar is required to get the scheme's benefits, including the loan, interest subvention and credit guarantee.
Not eligible:
- Education loans for admissions under management quota are not eligible.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Benefits
- Education loans without any collateral and without a guarantor, from scheduled commercial banks, regional rural banks and cooperative banks.
- Loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh carry a 75% credit guarantee from the Government of India through NCGTC, which encourages banks to lend.
- Interest subvention of 3% during the moratorium period on loans up to Rs 10 lakh for students whose annual family income is up to Rs 8 lakh.
- Separately, students with annual family income up to Rs 4.5 lakh in professional or technical courses get full interest subvention during the moratorium on loans up to Rs 10 lakh under the existing PM-USP CSIS scheme, also claimed through this portal.
- The interest rate is capped at each bank's External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) plus 0.5%.
- One application can be sent to up to 3 banks at the same time.

PM-Vidyalaxmi Scheme (Pradhan Mantri Vidyalaxmi) (PM-Vidyalaxmi) — Overview
Bank education loans with no collateral and no guarantor for students admitted to quality higher education institutions identified by the government. Loans up to Rs 7.5 lakh carry a 75% government credit guarantee, and students from families earning up to Rs 8 lakh a year can get 3% interest subvention. The Union Cabinet approved the scheme on 6 November 2024, and students apply on the PM-Vidyalaxmi portal.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Education (Department of Higher Education), with the Department of Financial Services.

question: I am from an OBC family earning under Rs 2 lakh a year and I am in Class 9 at a government school. What scholarship can I get from the government?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and Others (PM YASASVI) (PM YASASVI) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Belongs to the OBC, EBC (economically backward class) or DNT (denotified, nomadic or semi-nomadic tribe) category, with a valid certificate.
- EBC and DNT students qualify only if they are not already covered as SC, ST or OBC.
- Parents' or guardians' annual income from all sources must be Rs 2,50,000 or less.
- Indian nationals only.
- Pre-matric part: studying full-time in Class 9 or 10 in a government school.
- Post-matric part: has passed Class 10 or higher and is studying a recognised post-matric course in India (such as Class 11-12, ITI, diploma, graduation or post-graduation).
- Top class school part: studying in Class 9 to 12 at a school notified as a Top Class School; scholarships go by state-wise merit lists, with at least 30% for girls.
- Top class college part: admitted to a full-time course at a notified top class institution (such as an IIT, IIM, AIIMS, NIT or National Law University); scholarships go by merit within each institute's slots, with 30% of slots for girls.
Not eligible:
- Pre-matric and post-matric: only two boys from the same parents can get the scholarship; there is no such limit for girls.

PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and Others (PM YASASVI) (PM YASASVI) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Top class college: the benefit is not given to more than 2 siblings in a family.
- A student cannot hold another scholarship for the same purpose at the same time and must choose one.
- Post-matric: seats filled through management quota, NRI quota or spot admission are not eligible.
- Post-matric: a second course at the same level in another subject (for example B.Com after B.A.) is not covered.

PM Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs and Others (PM YASASVI) (PM YASASVI) — Overview
An umbrella scholarship scheme for OBC, EBC and DNT students whose family income is up to Rs 2.5 lakh a year. It covers pre-matric (Class 9-10) and post-matric (Class 11 onward) scholarships run by states, plus full-cost scholarships at notified top class schools and colleges applied for on the National Scholarship Portal.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Backward Classes Division).

question: My family lives in a village in a kutcha mud house and we cannot afford to build a pucca house. Is there any government help for us?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Eligibility rules
- You must live in a rural area (a village).
- Your household has no house, or lives in a kutcha house.
- Your present house has no more than 2 rooms.
- No member of your household owns a pucca house.
- Families are chosen from the SECC 2011 housing-deprivation data and the Awaas+ survey lists, and the Gram Sabha checks the list.
- These families get top priority (automatic inclusion): those with no shelter, destitute families living on alms, manual scavengers, Primitive Tribal Group families and legally freed bonded labourers.
Not eligible:
- Anyone in the household owns a motorised three-wheeler or four-wheeler, or mechanised three- or four-wheeler farm equipment.
- Anyone in the household has a Kisan Credit Card with a limit of Rs 50,000 or more.
- Any household member is a government employee, or the household runs a non-farm business registered with the government.
- Any household member earns more than Rs 15,000 a month.
- Anyone in the household pays income tax or professional tax.
- The household owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Benefits
- Rs 1.20 lakh to build a pucca house in plain areas.
- Rs 1.30 lakh in hill states and UTs (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh), North-Eastern states, difficult areas and IAP districts.
- Up to 90/95 days of unskilled wage work under MGNREGS for building your own house, on top of the grant.
- Rs 12,000 for a toilet, through Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), MGNREGS or another funding source.
- The house must be at least 25 square metres, with a space for clean cooking. Officials also help with house designs and trained masons.
- If you want one, officials help you get a bank loan of up to Rs 70,000. All payments go by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.

Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) — Overview
PMAY-G gives money to poor rural families who have no house or live in a kutcha house so they can build a pucca house. The grant is Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hill, north-eastern and difficult areas. The scheme is still running: its second phase adds 2 crore more houses, and the overall target is 4.95 crore houses by March 2029.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Rural Development (Department of Rural Development).

question: गाँव में हमारा कच्चा मकान है और पक्का घर बनाने के पैसे नहीं हैं, क्या सरकार से घर बनाने के लिए मदद मिल सकती है?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family lives in an urban area (a statutory town or a notified planning or development area).
- No member of your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.
- Your annual household income is up to Rs 9 lakh (Rs 9,00,000). EWS means up to Rs 3 lakh, LIG means Rs 3 lakh to Rs 6 lakh, and MIG means Rs 6 lakh to Rs 9 lakh.
- 'Family' means husband, wife and unmarried sons and/or unmarried daughters.
- Only EWS families (income up to Rs 3 lakh) can get help to build a house on their own land (BLC) or to own a house in a partnership project (AHP). For BLC you need your own land or a land patta from the state.
- The home-loan interest subsidy (ISS) is for EWS, LIG and MIG families. The loan must be up to Rs 25 lakh, the house worth up to Rs 35 lakh and the carpet area up to 120 sq m, and the loan must be sanctioned and paid out on or after 1 September 2024.
- Every family member must have Aadhaar or an Aadhaar Virtual ID.
Not eligible:
- You cannot apply if you were given a house under any Central, State or local government housing scheme in the last 20 years, in a town or a village.
- You cannot apply if your family owns a pucca house anywhere in India.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Families whose PMAY-U houses were cancelled (curtailed) after 31 December 2023 cannot get them sanctioned again under PMAY-U 2.0.
- No interest subsidy if the loan is above Rs 25 lakh or the house is worth more than Rs 35 lakh.
- No interest subsidy if an earlier owner already took the subsidy on the same property, or if you claim it again after moving your loan to another lender.

Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) — Benefits
- Building your own house (BLC) or a house in a partnership project (AHP): in most states you get Rs 1.5 lakh from the Centre plus at least Rs 1 lakh from the State, so Rs 2.5 lakh in all.
- In North-Eastern states, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Puducherry and Delhi, the Centre pays Rs 2.25 lakh and the State at least Rs 0.25 lakh. In other UTs the Centre pays Rs 2.50 lakh.
- BLC money is paid by DBT in 3 instalments (40:40:20) as building work goes ahead. The house must be 30 to 45 sq m.
- Home loans (ISS): you get a 4% interest subsidy on the first Rs 8 lakh of the loan, for up to 12 years. The maximum is Rs 1.80 lakh, paid in 5 yearly instalments into your loan account.
- Rental housing (ARH): affordable rented homes and dormitories for urban poor, working women, industrial workers and other EWS/LIG families.
- The house is put in the name of the woman head of the family, or jointly with her husband. It cannot be sold or transferred for 5 years.

question: How much overdraft can I get in a PM Jan Dhan Yojana account?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) — Eligibility rules
- Any Indian citizen who is eligible to open an ordinary bank account can open a basic savings account under the scheme.
- The account is meant for people who do not already have a bank account.
- Since 2018 the scheme aims to reach every adult without a bank account, not just one account per household.
- The overdraft facility is only for account holders aged 18 to 65 years.
- An overdraft of up to Rs 2,000 has no conditions attached; for larger amounts the bank looks at how the account has been run, usually over 6 months.
Not eligible:
- Account holders younger than 18 or older than 65 cannot get the overdraft.

Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) — Benefits
- A basic savings bank account with no minimum balance requirement, and interest on the money deposited.
- A free RuPay debit card.
- Accident insurance cover of Rs 2 lakh through the RuPay card for accounts opened after 28 August 2018 (Rs 1 lakh for accounts opened before that date).
- An overdraft of up to Rs 10,000 for eligible account holders.
- The account can receive Direct Benefit Transfers and can be used to join PMJJBY, PMSBY, Atal Pension Yojana and MUDRA loans.
- To claim the RuPay accident cover, the card should have been used for at least one transaction in the 90 days before the accident, and the claim should be reported to the bank within 90 days of the accident.

Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) — Overview
A national mission that helps people with no bank account open a basic savings account with no minimum balance. Account holders get a free RuPay debit card with accident insurance, and eligible holders can get an overdraft of up to Rs 10,000. The scheme started on 28 August 2014 and is still open.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services.

Sukanya Samriddhi Account Scheme (SSY) — Eligibility rules

- A third girl in the same family cannot get an account unless the extra girls are twins or triplets from the first or second birth.

question: How much money does PMMVY give for the first child?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Eligibility rules
- Open to pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.
- The woman must be between 18 years 7 months and 55 years old when the child is born.
- She must belong to at least one listed disadvantaged group: SC or ST, disabled (40% or more), BPL ration card, NFSA ration card, Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, e-Shram card, PM Kisan farmer, or MGNREGA job card.
- A net family income below Rs 8 lakh a year also counts as a qualifying group, even if none of the other groups apply.
- Pregnant or breastfeeding Anganwadi workers, Anganwadi helpers and ASHAs also qualify.
- The benefit covers the first child, and also the second child if the second child is a girl.
- For the second-child benefit, the pregnancy must be registered before delivery. The rules apply to births from 1 April 2022.
- The woman needs an Aadhaar number and a bank or post office account linked to Aadhaar.
Not eligible:
- Women with regular jobs in the Central Government, a State Government or a public sector undertaking cannot apply.
- Women who already get similar maternity benefits under another law cannot apply.
- There is no payment if the second child is a boy, and none for a third or later child.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Overview
PMMVY gives cash to pregnant women and new mothers from disadvantaged groups. They get Rs 5,000 in two instalments for the first child, and Rs 6,000 in one instalment if the second child is a girl. The money is paid straight into the woman's Aadhaar-linked bank or post office account.
Central government scheme. Ministry of Women and Child Development.

Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana (PMMVY) — Benefits
- First child: Rs 5,000 in two instalments.
- First instalment of Rs 3,000 once the pregnancy is registered and at least one ante-natal check-up is done within 6 months of the last menstrual period.
- Second instalment of Rs 2,000 once the birth is registered and the baby has had the first round of vaccines (BCG, OPV, DPT and Hepatitis-B), which are due by 14 weeks.
- Second child who is a girl: Rs 6,000 in one instalment after the birth, once she has had all vaccines due up to 14 weeks.
- If the second pregnancy gives twins or more and at least one baby is a girl, the second-girl benefit is paid.
- After a miscarriage or stillbirth, the woman counts as a new beneficiary in her next pregnancy.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the KALIA scheme for farmers in Odisha?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- Your family must own cultivable land, and the names must be entered in the state or UT land records.
- For this scheme a farmer family means husband, wife and minor children.
- There is no upper limit on land size; the original 2-hectare cap was dropped when the scheme was opened to all landholding farmer families.
- Eligibility is judged on land ownership recorded as on 01.02.2019; land received later by inheritance after the owner's death still counts, but land bought or gifted after that date does not make the new owner eligible.
- An Aadhaar number and a bank account seeded with Aadhaar are compulsory.
- e-KYC must be completed before payments are released.
- In some North-Eastern states and in Jharkhand, land certificates from village authorities or verified lineage records are accepted where regular land records do not exist.
Not eligible:
- Institutional landholders, and (for newly added beneficiaries) Non-Resident Indians as defined under the Income Tax Act.
- Families where any member holds or has held a constitutional post, or is or was a Union or State minister, MP, MLA, MLC, mayor of a municipal corporation or chairperson of a district panchayat.

Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- Families where any member is a serving or retired officer or employee of the Central or State Government, a central or state PSU or a government autonomous body, or a regular employee of a local body; Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D staff are not excluded.
- Families with a retired pensioner whose monthly pension is Rs 10,000 or more (Multi Tasking Staff, Class IV and Group D pensioners are not excluded).
- Families where any member paid income tax in the last assessment year.
- Families with a practising professional registered with a professional body: doctor, engineer, lawyer, chartered accountant or architect.

Kisan Credit Card (KCC) Scheme with Modified Interest Subvention Scheme (MISS) (KCC) — Eligibility rules
- Farmers who own and cultivate land, either alone or jointly.
- Tenant farmers, oral lessees and sharecroppers.
- Self Help Groups or Joint Liability Groups of farmers, including groups of tenant farmers and sharecroppers.
- Dairy, poultry, sheep, goat, pig and rabbit farmers with their own, rented or leased sheds, individually, jointly or in groups.
- Fishers and fish farmers who own or lease a pond, tank, open water body, hatchery or registered fishing boat and hold the required fishing licence.
Not eligible:
- Only one KCC per farmer: the application asks you to declare that you have no KCC from another bank branch.
- If you already have a combined KCC for crops and allied activities, a separate livestock or fisheries KCC is not issued; the existing limit is raised instead.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the Rythu Bharosa scheme of Telangana?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY) — Eligibility rules
- Must be a senior citizen aged 60 years or above.
- Must belong to the BPL category, shown by a BPL ration card, proof of old age pension under IGNOAPS or a state/UT pension scheme, or a certificate from the district authority.
- Seniors who are not BPL can also apply if their monthly income from all sources is Rs 15,000 or less.
- Must have an age-related disability or infirmity, such as low vision, hearing loss, loss of teeth or difficulty in walking.
- Must have an Aadhaar card or Aadhaar enrolment slip.
- A medical officer's certificate is needed for loss of vision, hearing impairment, loss of teeth, or locomotor disability needing a wheelchair.
Not eligible:
- People below 60 years of age.
- Non-BPL seniors whose monthly income from all sources is more than Rs 15,000.
- Anyone who received the same device free from any government source (including local bodies and public undertakings) in the last 3 years.

Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (NPY) — Eligibility rules
- You must be a TB (tuberculosis) patient who is notified (registered) on the Ni-kshay portal.
- Patients treated in the private sector qualify too, as long as they are notified on Ni-kshay.
- New, previously treated and drug-resistant TB patients are all covered.
- There is no age or income limit; all notified TB patients are beneficiaries.
- Children with TB are covered; if the child has no bank account, the money goes to a parent's or guardian's account.
- Patients notified on or after 1 April 2018, and those already on treatment on that date, are eligible.
Not eligible:
- A TB patient who is not notified on the Ni-kshay portal cannot receive the payment.
- Payments are only for the period the patient is on anti-TB treatment; they stop when treatment ends.

Viksit Bharat – Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) — Eligibility rules
- The household lives in a rural area. The guarantee applies in all rural areas of India from 1 July 2026.
- Work is given to adult members, meaning people who have completed 18 years of age.
- Adult members must be willing to do unskilled manual work.
- The household needs a Gramin Rozgar Guarantee Card. Existing MGNREGA job cards with completed e-KYC stay valid until the new cards are issued.
Not eligible:
- Households in urban areas are not covered; the Act applies only to rural areas.
- Persons below 18 years of age cannot be given work under the scheme.

question: What are the eligibility rules for the Mukhyamantri Kanya Sumangala Yojana of Uttar Pradesh?
answer:
These are the official rules that match your question. Please check them against your own details. The final decision is made by the government office.

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 1 of 2)
- You must be a pregnant woman who gives birth in a health facility: a sub-centre, PHC, CHC, FRU, the general ward of a district or state hospital, or an accredited private institution.
- In the 10 Low Performing States (Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Assam, Rajasthan, Odisha, Jammu and Kashmir), every pregnant woman who delivers in a government health centre qualifies.
- In all other states and UTs (called High Performing States), only women from BPL, Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe families qualify.
- In every state, BPL, SC and ST women also qualify if they deliver in an accredited private institution, but they must show a BPL or SC/ST certificate and a referral slip.
- In the Low Performing States there is no age limit and no limit on the number of births for delivery in a government or accredited facility.
Not eligible:
- In the High Performing States, women who are not BPL, SC or ST do not get the cash payment.
- Births in a private hospital that is not accredited for JSY are not covered.

Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) — Eligibility rules (part 2 of 2)
- The government does not pay the bill of a private hospital; a woman who chooses an accredited private hospital gets only her fixed cash amount.

Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY) — Eligibility rules
- The applicant must be a woman who is at least 18 years old.
- No one in the household should already have an LPG connection from any oil marketing company.
- The household must fall in one of the listed groups: SC or ST households, PMAY-Gramin beneficiaries, Most Backward Classes, Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) card holders, tea and ex-tea garden tribes, forest dwellers, people living on islands or river islands, or SECC (AHL TIN) households.
- A poor household outside these groups can still qualify by giving a 14-point deprivation declaration in the set format.
- Migrant families can apply by giving a self-declaration in place of address proof and a ration card.
Not eligible:
- Households where any family member already has an LPG connection.
- Women under 18 years of age.
- Men cannot get the connection in their own name; it is issued to an adult woman of the household.
